transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I just feel worn out all the time. It's like, even after a full night in bed, my body feels like it's made of sandbags. Getting through a workday takes absolutely everything I have right now. I work in market research, and lately we've been running these focus groups for a new line of organic pet food. It's actually wild how much money people will spend on their dogs. My sister has this labradoodle that gets custom meals delivered, and it comes in these little insulated boxes packed with dry ice. Have you ever seen those? The dry ice makes that really cool fog if you put it in the sink, though you have to be careful not to touch it with your bare hands because it'll burn you. 

But, um, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the tiredness. Yeah, doing my job or even just folding laundry takes everything I have. I just stare at the basket.
How long have you been feeling this kind of tiredness?

I'd say this really heavy, exhausted, slowed-down feeling has been going on most days for about the past two months. 

Actually, two months ago is right around when my husband and I bought our new mattress. It's one of those memory foam ones you buy online that comes vacuum-sealed in a cardboard box, which is just crazy to me. You cut the plastic and it just expands like a life raft. We had to upgrade to a king size because our cat, Barnaby, insists on sleeping right between us. He's a Maine Coon, so he's absolutely massive, and he snores exactly like a grown man. I actually took a video of it to show the vet because I was worried he had feline sleep apnea or something, if that's even a thing... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, about two months of just feeling completely drained most days.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days since you started feeling this tiredness?

Yeah, I really have. Most days I wake up with this... just this heavy, flat feeling right in my chest. It's like I can't shake it. I'll just sit at the kitchen table, staring out at the yard, and I just feel like there is absolutely no good version of the future coming. 

Which is a shame, honestly, because we actually just had the yard redone. We hired this local landscaping company to put in drought-resistant plants because our summer water bill was getting completely ridiculous. They planted all this lavender and Russian sage, which smells amazing when it rains, but it attracts so many bees. I don't mind bees, you know, save the bees and all that, but our neighbor's kid is highly allergic. He has to carry an EpiPen everywhere he goes, poor thing. His mom bought him this little insulated belt pouch for it so the medicine doesn't get ruined in the summer heat, which I didn't even know was a thing you had to worry about... 

Wait, did I answer your question? I'm sorry, my brain just keeps wandering off today. What did you ask me about? Oh, right, feeling down. Yeah, just really flat and heavy most days.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before you started feeling this way?

No, not really. I used to do a lot, actually. I'd make time for hiking, yoga, working in the garden, taking bird photos... but lately I just keep canceling on people. My camera is just sitting in the closet gathering dust because none of it feels worth the effort right now. 

It's a really nice camera, too. It's a mirrorless one my husband got me for our anniversary a couple of years ago. We actually went to this incredible bed and breakfast up in the mountains for that anniversary, and they served these homemade blueberry scones every morning that were just out of this world. The owner said her secret was freezing the butter before grating it into the flour, which I had never heard of before. I tried it once when we got home, but my kitchen gets so warm in the summer that the butter just melted anyway, and it made this huge mess on the counter. I ended up having to use this special citrus cleaner to get the grease off, and it smelled like oranges for a week...

I'm sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was the question? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I just don't have the energy or the interest for my hobbies anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite since you started feeling this way?

No, I don't think so. My appetite has been pretty normal, honestly. I'm eating about the same amount I usually do. 

My husband usually does most of the grocery shopping anyway, mostly at that organic market downtown. They have this really great bulk section, which I love, but they recently completely rearranged all their aisles. I went in there the other day to get our regular coffee beans and I couldn't find a single thing. I actually ended up talking to the store manager about their layout, because I'm a market research analyst, so I just can't help but notice when customer flow is completely disrupted like that. I was trying to explain to him how putting the high-traffic items all the way in the back corner creates this terrible bottleneck right by the dairy case, but he just looked at me like I was speaking another language. It reminded me of this focus group we ran for a beverage company last year, and they absolutely refused to listen when we told them people hated their new bottle shape because it wouldn't fit in a standard car cup holder... 

Oh, gosh, I'm so sorry. I completely lost the thread again. What did you ask me? Was it about food? Oh, right, my appetite. No, no real changes there. It's been pretty much the same.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since you started feeling this way?

No, I wouldn't say I've had trouble sleeping. I mean, I go to bed around the same time I always do, and I sleep through the night fine. 

Actually, we just bought a new mattress a few months ago, which might be helping. It's one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box. It was so heavy, the delivery guy just left it on the porch and my husband and I had to drag it up the stairs ourselves. It took us like twenty minutes just to get it around the landing. We ended up scuffing the paint on the wall, which was so frustrating because we literally just painted that hallway this soft gray color. Finding the right gray is surprisingly difficult, you know? They all either look too blue or too purple once you get them on the wall. We must have bought like ten different sample pots before we settled on this one called 'Morning Fog.' The guy at the hardware store was starting to recognize me...

Wait, I'm sorry. I'm rambling again. Did you ask about my sleep? Yeah, no, my sleep has been totally normal. No problems there.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

Yeah, I do. A lot, actually. It's... well, we refinanced our house recently to pull some money out, and I just keep replaying that mortgage decision over and over in my head. I keep telling myself I was so selfish and reckless, like I put our whole household at risk. My husband keeps reminding me we made the decision together, but I just can't shake this feeling that I ruined everything.

We used a local credit union for the refinance, actually, because their rates were just a tiny bit lower than the big banks. The loan officer we worked with was this really sweet guy named Greg. He had all these pictures of his golden retrievers on his desk. He breeds them, apparently, and he was telling us how the waiting list for one of his puppies is like two years long. I've always wanted a dog, but our yard isn't fenced, and getting a fence installed right now is just outrageously expensive. Lumber prices have been so crazy since the pandemic. We looked into getting a vinyl fence instead, but the HOA has all these strict rules about what materials you can use, and they have to approve the color and everything. It's such a headache dealing with the HOA board. The president is this retired guy who just walks around with a clipboard all day measuring people's grass...

I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry, I don't know why I can't stay on track today. You asked about feeling guilty, right? Yeah, the mortgage thing. I just feel so terrible about it, even when my husband says it's fine.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to live or hurting yourself since you started feeling this way?

Well... yes. Sometimes. Especially late at night when everything is quiet, I catch myself thinking that my husband might just be better off without me. I haven't made a plan or anything like that, but the thought just keeps coming back, and it honestly scares me. 

He works so hard, you know? He's a project manager for this mid-sized logistics company, and they've had him working crazy hours lately because they're transitioning to this entirely new inventory tracking software. He was telling me about it the other night—it's cloud-based, which is supposed to be more secure, but the migration process has been a total nightmare for them. They had to hire this outside consulting firm just to manage the data transfer, and apparently, the lead consultant is this guy who insists on having three-hour Zoom meetings every single morning. I don't know how anyone gets any actual work done with that many meetings. It reminds me of when my firm tried to switch our survey analytics platform a few years ago. We ended up losing like three months of demographic data because someone didn't map the server drives correctly... 

Oh, wow, I'm doing it again. I'm so sorry. My brain is just everywhere. But to answer your question... yes. The thoughts about him being better off without me. They do happen, and it's really frightening when they do.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and fidgety?

Well, my husband actually said something about that the other day. He told me I've been moving around the house like I'm underwater. And I guess he's right, even when he asks me a simple question, it feels like it takes me forever just to get the words out. They just come out so slowly. 

It's kind of like how our internet connection has been acting lately. We switched providers last month because they were running this promotion where you get a free year of some streaming service, but the router they gave us is just awful. It drops the signal right in the middle of the day, which is so frustrating when I'm trying to work from home. I had to call their customer service, and I swear I was on hold for forty-five minutes listening to this terrible elevator music. It was a cover of "Girl from Ipanema" but played on a synthesizer, if you can imagine that. When I finally got a real person, he told me I needed to upgrade to their premium mesh network package. I feel like that's how they get you, you know? They lure you in with the cheap introductory rate and then nickel and dime you for the equipment that actually works...

Oh, I'm so sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. What were we talking about? Oh, right, moving slowly. Yeah, it's just... everything feels heavy and slow right now. Like I'm underwater.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight since you started feeling this way?

No, I don't think so. My clothes still fit the same, so I haven't really lost any weight. I've mostly just been heating up quick things lately, honestly. Like those frozen meals from Trader Joe's? They have this mandarin orange chicken that my husband really likes. Actually, my coworker Sarah was the one who told me about it. She works in the marketing department with me, but she runs this whole food blog on the side. She spends her entire weekend taking these perfectly styled photos of meals. She just bought this massive ring light on Amazon during Prime Day to get better lighting for her kitchen. Prime Day was so chaotic this year, wasn't it? The delivery vans were constantly blocking our street. One of the drivers actually backed right over my neighbor's mailbox. It was this beautiful custom brick mailbox, too, and it just completely crumbled. The neighbor was furious, he was out there taking pictures for the insurance claim and yelling on his cell phone...

Wait. I'm rambling again, aren't I? I am so sorry, my mind just keeps drifting off today. But to answer your question, no, I haven't noticed any significant weight loss.
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things?

Well, I wouldn't say I feel anxious or worried, exactly. Not more than usual, anyway. I mean, everyone worries a little bit, right? 

Like the other day, I was at the grocery store, and I realized I had left my reusable bags in the trunk of the car. I always try to bring them because our city just passed that new ordinance where they charge you ten cents for every paper bag. It's not even about the money, it's just the principle of it, you know? And the plastic ones are terrible for the environment. I watched this documentary on Netflix last month about ocean plastics, and it was just devastating. They showed these sea turtles that had gotten tangled up in soda rings. It makes you really think about where all our garbage goes. My sister actually volunteers at a marine wildlife rescue down in Florida. She moved there about five years ago because she couldn't stand the winters up here anymore. She bought this cute little condo right near the beach, but the homeowners association fees are absolutely ridiculous. They just raised them again because they had to repave the visitor parking lot, which took them three weeks to finish...

Oh, goodness. I did it again. I'm so sorry, I don't know why I keep doing that today. But no, I don't think I've been feeling particularly anxious or worried about things.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety at any point since you started feeling this way?

Well, no, not restless. Actually, it's more the opposite, like we were talking about earlier. My husband was just saying how I move around the house like I'm underwater. And he's right, even simple questions take me forever to answer because the words just come out so slowly. 

It's funny he said "underwater," though, because we actually went to the aquarium last weekend. They have this huge new shark tunnel exhibit that just opened up. We had to buy tickets weeks in advance because everyone wanted to see it. The line to get in wrapped all the way around the building, and it was so hot out. There was this poor family in front of us with twin toddlers who were just melting down. I felt so bad for the parents. They had one of those massive double strollers, the kind that take up the whole sidewalk? I don't know how people maneuver those things. My cousin had one for her kids, and she said it wouldn't even fit through the front door of her house unless she folded it up first. She ended up selling it on Facebook Marketplace after like two months. Facebook Marketplace is so weird now, isn't it? Half the time people say they want something and then they just ghost you, or they try to offer you way less than you're asking...

Oh, I'm sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? I just keep drifting. But no, not restless or fidgety. Just... really, really slow. Like I'm moving through molasses.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual most of the time?

Yeah, exactly like I was just saying a second ago! It really is most of the time. My husband is the one who keeps pointing it out, saying I move around the house like I'm underwater. And it's not just moving, it's talking too. He'll ask me something so simple, and it just takes me a while to answer because the words come out so slowly. 

Speaking of water, though, we actually had a pipe burst in our basement last winter, and it was an absolute nightmare. The plumber took three days to come out because there was a freeze warning and everyone's pipes were bursting all over the city. We had to rip up all the carpeting in the downstairs guest room. We ended up replacing it with that luxury vinyl plank flooring? It looks just like real wood but it's completely waterproof. My sister-in-law put it in her kitchen, but she chose this really dark espresso color that shows absolutely every speck of dust. She has two golden retrievers, so you can imagine the dog hair. They shed constantly. She actually bought one of those robot vacuums to keep up with it, but one of the dogs is absolutely terrified of it and barks at it the entire time it runs on its little schedule...

Oh, gosh. I'm doing it again. I am so sorry, my brain just will not stay on track today. But yes, to answer your question, I do feel like I'm moving much slower than usual most of the time.
Do you ever feel like you're fidgeting or can't sit still?

Well, right now, no, I'm just feeling really sluggish. But... actually, there was a point a few weeks ago where it was the complete opposite. I had this sudden burst where I literally could not sit still. I kept jumping up from my desk to sketch out new office layouts, and I reorganized all my files, and I just kept starting one more task even when there was absolutely no reason it had to be done right then. 

I was using those new pastel highlighters I bought online. They come in this pack of twelve, and the colors are so much softer than those glaring neon ones, you know? I saw them on a stationery blog I follow. The woman who runs it lives in Japan, and she reviews all these amazing pens and notebooks that you can't even get here in the States unless you pay a fortune for shipping. I tried to order a planner from there once, but it got stuck in customs for over a month. By the time it finally arrived, it was already February, and I had completely missed the whole "new year, fresh start" window. I ended up just giving it to my niece because she loves anything with grid paper. She's applying to architecture programs right now, which is so stressful. The acceptance rates at the schools she wants to go to are incredibly low, and they require this massive portfolio...

Oh, I'm so sorry. I did it again. I just can't seem to hold a thought straight today. But yes, a few weeks ago, I was incredibly fidgety and just could not stop moving or starting new projects.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but now you don't find pleasure in them anymore?

Yeah, actually. That's been a big thing lately. I used to make time for all these things I loved, like hiking and yoga, and I had this whole garden going. I also loved taking bird photos. But lately, I just keep canceling plans, and my camera is just sitting in the closet gathering dust because none of it feels worth the effort anymore. 

I bought that camera right before our trip to Costa Rica a few years ago. We stayed at this eco-lodge up in the cloud forest, and the wildlife was just incredible. You'd wake up and there would be toucans right outside the window. The coffee there was amazing, too. They grew it right on the property, and you could take a tour of the whole roasting process. I brought back like five bags of these whole beans, but then my grinder broke right after we got home. It was one of those cheap blade grinders, and I guess a rock got mixed in with the beans? It made this horrible screeching noise and just smoked. I meant to buy a nice burr grinder to replace it, but they're so expensive, and there are so many different kinds. I started reading reviews on all these coffee snob forums, and people get really intense about their grind size and water temperature...

Oh, gosh. I'm sorry. I'm drifting again, aren't I? But yeah, to answer your question, I just don't have the energy or interest for my hobbies right now. It all just feels like too much work.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Honestly... no. Not really. Like I was saying, I used to make time for hiking, yoga, my garden, and taking bird photos, but lately I keep canceling or letting my camera sit in the closet because none of it feels worth the effort. It's just... I can't even get excited about things I know I should like. 

Even my yoga mat is just rolled up under the bed. I got one of those really thick, extra-cushioned ones because the hardwood floors in our bedroom are so hard on my knees. We had the floors refinished last summer, and the fumes from the polyurethane were just awful. We had to stay at my sister's house for three days while it dried. She lives out in the suburbs, and the commute to work from there was a nightmare. Traffic on the interstate is always backed up past the river, especially since they started that bridge construction project. They say it's going to take two years to finish, which is ridiculous. The detour adds like twenty minutes to the drive, and the alternate route goes right past this old bakery that used to make the best sourdough bread. The guy who owned it retired last year, and his kids didn't want to take over the business, so they just sold the building to a developer. I think they're turning it into luxury condos, which is what they seem to be doing with every empty lot in the city these days. It's really changing the whole character of the neighborhood...

Oh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry. My brain is just... everywhere. But no, I really don't look forward to anything right now. It's all just... flat.
Have you been feeling jittery or had an inability to sit still recently?

No, definitely not jittery right now. If anything, it's the exact opposite. My husband actually pointed out the other day that I'm moving around the house like I'm underwater. And even when he asks me a simple question, it takes me a while to answer because the words just... they come out so slowly. 

He asked me what I wanted for dinner on Tuesday, and I just stared at him. We usually do taco Tuesdays, which started back when the kids were little and we needed something easy. I used to make my own salsa for it, with tomatoes from that garden I mentioned. I grew these amazing heirloom varieties—Cherokee Purples and Brandywine. The Brandywines get so huge, you have to stake them up really well or the branches just snap under the weight. I bought these heavy-duty tomato cages from a local nursery, the kind made from real galvanized steel, not that flimsy wire stuff you get at the big box stores. The owner of the nursery was this sweet older man who always wore a straw hat and gave me advice on keeping the aphids away. He swore by planting marigolds next to the tomatoes, which actually worked really well. The orange and yellow flowers looked so pretty, too. I tried saving the seeds from the marigolds one year to plant the next spring, but I didn't dry them out enough before I put them in the envelope, and they all got moldy. It was such a disappointment, especially because I had bought these special little glass jars with cork stoppers to keep all my seeds organized...

I'm sorry. I'm doing it again. I just keep losing my train of thought today. But no, I'm not jittery at all. Just really, really slow.
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, or heard voices that others cannot hear, since you started feeling this way?

No, nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or had any weird thoughts. It's just the slowness and the feeling like everything is pointless. 

It's kind of like how quiet the house gets when everyone is gone. My kids went to stay with my parents for a long weekend a while back, just to give me a break. My parents live out in the country, on this beautiful property with a big wrap-around porch. My dad built that porch himself, actually. He used to be a carpenter before he retired. He's always been so good with his hands. He made this gorgeous oak dining table for my sister when she got married. It seats twelve people, which is crazy because her dining room is tiny. They live in this historic row house downtown, and the rooms are all so narrow. The architecture is stunning, though, with all that exposed brick and original crown molding. But the parking is a nightmare. You have to have a residential permit, and even then, you end up parking three blocks away and walking in the rain. I ruined a perfectly good pair of suede boots doing that once. They were those really comfortable ankle boots with the little block heel, you know? I tried using that protective spray on them, but it just made the suede look all stiff and weird...

Sorry. I'm drifting again. But no, no voices or strange thoughts. Just my regular, rambling thoughts.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness?

Yeah. I mean, more than just feeling useless, it's this awful guilt. I keep replaying this decision we made about our mortgage, and I just keep telling myself how selfish and reckless I was. Like I put our whole household at risk. My husband keeps reminding me that we made the decision together, but I can't shake it. 

We refinanced to get a lower rate, but we ended up taking some cash out to fix the roof. The roof was a complete disaster. We had this huge storm roll through last spring—one of those weird microbursts or whatever the meteorologists call them. It knocked down the big oak tree in the Johnsons' yard next door. They were devastated because they planted that tree when their first daughter was born. She just graduated from college, actually. She went to school out of state, somewhere in Colorado, I think. She always loved skiing. I tried skiing once when I was in my twenties, but I have terrible balance. I ended up twisting my ankle on the bunny hill and spending the rest of the weekend sitting in the lodge drinking hot cocoa. The cocoa was really good, though—they made it with real melted chocolate instead of powder, and they had those giant, homemade marshmallows...

Oh, God. I'm sorry. I really am. I just... I can't stay on track. But yes, I feel incredibly guilty and worthless about the mortgage thing. It just eats at me all day.
Have you been feeling an internal restlessness or an inability to sit still?

No, not really. I mean, you asked me earlier if I was jittery, and it's still just the same. I'm not restless at all, just... heavy. 

It's actually a lot like how my grandmother used to describe her arthritis when the weather would change. She always knew when it was going to rain because her knees would ache so badly she could barely get out of her favorite armchair. It was this hideous floral print armchair from the seventies, green and orange with these big wooden armrests. She refused to get rid of it, even when my mom offered to buy her a brand new recliner for Christmas one year. My mom loves Christmas shopping. She starts in July, hunting for sales and hiding things in the attic. One year she forgot where she hid my brother's present—it was this remote control car he really wanted—and we didn't find it until we were cleaning out the attic to move three years later. We moved right before I started high school, which was terrifying. Being the new kid is awful. I had to eat lunch in the library for the first two weeks because I didn't know anyone, and the librarian, Mrs. Gable, would let me help her reshelve the mystery section...

Sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? But no, no internal restlessness. Just feeling like I can barely move.

patient.answer:
Well, I came in because I just feel worn out all the time. It's like, even after a full night in bed, my body feels like it's made of sandbags. Getting through a workday takes absolutely everything I have right now. I work in market research, and lately we've been running these focus groups for a new line of organic pet food. It's actually wild how much money people will spend on their dogs. My sister has this labradoodle that gets custom meals delivered, and it comes in these little insulated boxes packed with dry ice. Have you ever seen those? The dry ice makes that really cool fog if you put it in the sink, though you have to be careful not to touch it with your bare hands because it'll burn you. 

But, um, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the tiredness. Yeah, doing my job or even just folding laundry takes everything I have. I just stare at the basket.

patient.answer:
I'd say this really heavy, exhausted, slowed-down feeling has been going on most days for about the past two months. 

Actually, two months ago is right around when my husband and I bought our new mattress. It's one of those memory foam ones you buy online that comes vacuum-sealed in a cardboard box, which is just crazy to me. You cut the plastic and it just expands like a life raft. We had to upgrade to a king size because our cat, Barnaby, insists on sleeping right between us. He's a Maine Coon, so he's absolutely massive, and he snores exactly like a grown man. I actually took a video of it to show the vet because I was worried he had feline sleep apnea or something, if that's even a thing... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, about two months of just feeling completely drained most days.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I really have. Most days I wake up with this... just this heavy, flat feeling right in my chest. It's like I can't shake it. I'll just sit at the kitchen table, staring out at the yard, and I just feel like there is absolutely no good version of the future coming. 

Which is a shame, honestly, because we actually just had the yard redone.
